problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Strict feasibility in bilinear parameters w=(v,s): find s⟨a_i,v⟩>0 for every i. The feasible set in (v,s) is generally nonconvex; no optimization objective is explicitly specified.

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Finite-data homogeneous separation: n=count≥1 hidden vectors satisfy ‖a_i‖≤R and ⟨u,a_i⟩≥γ for some hidden unit vector u, with 0<γ≤R.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: Query (i,(v,s)) returns the exact gradient (s a_i,⟨a_i,v⟩) of the component margin s⟨a_i,v⟩. Replies have no oracle error or history dependence. Each complete scan costs n oracle calls.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/NoisyBatchQuadraticPerceptron.lean: Query, answer, spec.admissible, family; LongTails/Template.lean: executeWithTrace.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: Each component query also returns its exact scalar margin s⟨a_i,v⟩.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Features lie in ℝ^d and weights in ℝ^d×ℝ with the Euclidean product norm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The prescribed family scans all components at one fixed point, then updates w←w+(η/n)Σ_{i:s⟨a_i,v⟩≤0}(s a_i,⟨a_i,v⟩)+σξ_k whenever a violation exists. Here η>0 is fixed, σ>0, and ξ_k are independent standard Gaussian vectors in ℝ^{d+1}. A violation-free scan freezes the point. Noise is algorithmic, not oracle error. Public inputs are d,n,R,γ,σ,start and the noise source; the data and separating witness are hidden. Failure probability δ is not supplied to the algorithm constructor.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/NoisyBatchQuadraticPerceptron.lean: Public, Params, scanUpdate, family, spec.valid, spec.publicInput; LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: IID; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The output must strictly separate every datum: s⟨a_i,v⟩>0 for all i. There is no positive output-margin threshold or approximate objective criterion. Output is the current point after the fixed oracle budget.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/NoisyBatchQuadraticPerceptron.lean: Separates, family, spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: execute, Convergence.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: For every admissible dataset, the probability that any output margin is nonpositive is at most δ=failure, where 0<δ<1.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The formulation combines bilinear strict separation with a prescribed full-scan update, persistent isotropic Gaussian weight perturbations, and freezing upon verified separation. Repository proofs and implementations were not inspected; the literature search does not certify novelty.

descriptionHtml:
Noisy Batch Quadratic Perceptron

We consider strict separation of vectors a1,…,an∈Rd, where n≥1 and d≥0 are integers, by quadratic weights x=(v,s)∈Rd×R. The vectors are bounded and share a unit separating direction with positive margin. At a query (i,x), the oracle returns the margin s⟨ai,v⟩ and direction (sai,⟨ai,v⟩). We analyze the noisy batch quadratic perceptron, initialized at a given point, with independent standard Gaussian perturbations scaled by σ>0. For δ∈(0,1), the goal is an output x¯=(v¯,s¯) satisfying s¯⟨ai,v¯⟩>0 for every i with probability at least 1−δ.

Equip the weight space E=Rd×R with the Euclidean product norm ∥(v,s)∥2=∥v∥22+s2. For each data vector, define its quadratic margin and update direction by mi(v,s)=s⟨ai,v⟩,gi(v,s)=(sai,⟨ai,v⟩). The task is to find x∈E such that mi(x)>0 for all i∈{1,…,n}. The algorithm receives d, n, a radius R, a margin γ, the noise scale σ, the starting point x0∈E, and the prescribed noise source; only the oracle-call budget may additionally depend on δ.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Bounded separable data). The parameters satisfy 0<γ≤R. There exists u∈Rd such that ∥u∥2=1,∥ai∥2≤R,⟨u,ai⟩≥γ,i=1,…,n.

Assumption 2 (Gaussian perturbations). The prescribed noise source consists of a probability space (Ω,F,ν) and measurable maps Zk:Ω→E, k≥0. Under ν, these maps are mutually independent and satisfy Zk∼N(0,Id+1),k≥0, where Id+1 is the identity on E. The perturbation scale satisfies σ>0.

Queries may use any index i∈{1,…,n} and any weight x∈E. The oracle returns the exact pair (mi(x),gi(x)); the Gaussian noise enters the weight updates.

Our formulation is algorithm-specific: we analyze the noisy batch quadratic perceptron. The method chooses a fixed step size η>0 from its available inputs and starts at the given x0. During batch k, it queries indices 1,…,n in order at the unchanged weight xk. Define Vk={i∈{1,…,n}:mi(xk)≤0}. The accumulator starts at zero and adds gi(xk) exactly when i∈Vk. After a complete scan with Vk≠∅, the method updates xk+1=xk+ηn∑i∈Vkgi(xk)+σZk. It then resets the accumulator and begins the next scan at index 1. If a complete scan has Vk=∅, the method freezes at xk: subsequent calls repeat the last query (n,xk) and leave the weight unchanged. No perturbation is applied on such a scan.

Each complete scan uses n oracle calls. For a prescribed total budget N∈N, the output x¯ is the current weight after those calls. An incomplete final scan does not change the weight, and calls made after freezing still count toward N. The output must satisfy P(∃i∈{1,…,n}:mi(x¯)≤0)≤δ, where P is the law of the algorithm’s randomness, realizing the prescribed noise source.

comparisonHtml:
Signed data a1,…,an∈Rd, n≥1, satisfy ∥ai∥≤R and ⟨u,ai⟩≥δ for some ∥u∥=1, with 0<δ≤R. The setup requires averaged full-batch quadratic perceptron updates for w=(c,v), arbitrary w0, and IID N(0,Id+1) perturbations scaled by fixed σ>0, freezing after a successful scan. Result (1) uses η=δ/[8(n+1)R2]. Target: P{∃i: v⟨ai,c⟩≤0}≤ρ, 0<ρ<1. One call returns v⟨ai,c⟩ and (vai,⟨ai,c⟩).

Comparison for NoisyBatchQuadraticPerceptron.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) NoisyBatchQuadraticPerceptronGlobal (Ours) (review) O(nρ[n2R2δ2+∥w0∥2(d+1)σ2]⋅(2ρ)H)
(2) Data recovery + linear feasibility; derived bound (LongTails, n.d.) O(n) calls; deterministic. Query (c,v)=(0,1) to recover every ai; solve offline. (1): No established improvement in classification cost, data scope, or output. (2) uses the same oracle but falls outside the prescribed family. (1) has larger cost throughout the domain and allows failure probability ρ; (2) assumes unrestricted offline computation.
(3) Cyclic perceptron (Novikoff 1962); derived scan cost O(n[1+R2/δ2]) calls; deterministic, initialized at zero. Queries (x,1) use the same oracle. (1): No established improvement in classification cost or scope. (3) uses linear updates outside the prescribed family; arbitrary initialization also converges. (1) adds dimension, noise, initialization and confidence dependence; its displayed cost is worse. The arbitrary-start bound for (3) adds initialization dependence.
(4) Two-sample noisy QPA (Tyurin 2026, Theorem 5.1, v2) O(tL[1+log⁡(tL)]) per-example convolutional calls, success probability 1−ρ; n=2, dataset (5), kernel k=2. (1): Method-specific global convergence for arbitrary n, separable data, w0 and fixed σ>0 in the width-one model; frozen output eventually constant almost surely. Rates not comparable: different models. (4) requires 0<μ≤1/10, nonzero initial projection and theorem-tuned noise; its acceleration is not established for (1).

Abbr: QPA: quadratic perceptron algorithm; H=5exp(25000(d+1)2(n+1)4R4/δ4). For (4), a1=1, a2=−(1+μe1), t=d/μ, q=∥θ0∥2/|⟨θ0,vμ,+⟩|2, and L=[1+log⁡(q/ρ3)][1+log⁡(tq)]; vμ,+ is the unit eigenvector of the second sample’s convolutional matrix with eigenvalue μ, and θ0 its initial weight. log denotes the natural logarithm. Costs count all per-example calls, including full scans; offline arithmetic is not counted.

source:
import LongTails.Setups.TwoSampleQuadraticPerceptron
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.ProdL2
import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.Multivariate

open MeasureTheory OracleTemplate
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.NoisyBatchQuadraticPerceptron

abbrev Features := TwoSampleQuadraticPerceptron.Features
abbrev Weights (d : ℕ) := WithLp 2 (Features d × ℝ)

structure NoiseSource (d : ℕ) where
  Ω : Type
  measurableSpace : MeasurableSpace Ω
  law : @ProbabilityMeasure Ω measurableSpace
  sample : ℕ → Ω → Weights d

attribute [instance] NoiseSource.measurableSpace

structure Public where
  dimension : ℕ
  count : ℕ+
  radius : ℝ
  margin : ℝ
  noiseScale : ℝ
  start : Weights dimension
  noise : NoiseSource dimension

structure Params where
  input : Public
  failure : ℝ

abbrev Data (P : Public) := Fin P.count → Features P.dimension
abbrev Query (P : Public) := Fin P.count × Weights P.dimension

structure Reply (d : ℕ) where
  margin : ℝ
  direction : Weights d

noncomputable def answer {d : ℕ} (a : Features d) (w : Weights d) : Reply d where
  margin := w.ofLp.2 * ⟪a, w.ofLp.1⟫
  direction := WithLp.toLp 2 (w.ofLp.2 • a, ⟪a, w.ofLp.1⟫)

def Separates {P : Public} (data : Data P) (w : Weights P.dimension) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, 0 < w.ofLp.2 * ⟪data i, w.ofLp.1⟫

structure ScanState (P : Public) where
  seed : P.noise.Ω
  point : Weights P.dimension
  accumulator : Weights P.dimension
  violated : Bool
  cursor : Fin P.count
  batch : ℕ
  frozen : Bool

noncomputable def initial (P : Public) (ω : P.noise.Ω) : ScanState P :=
  ⟨ω, P.start, 0, false, ⟨0, P.count.pos⟩, 0, false⟩

noncomputable def scanUpdate (P : Public) (η : ℝ) (s : ScanState P)
    (reply : Reply P.dimension) : ScanState P :=
  if s.frozen then s else
    let wrong := decide (reply.margin ≤ 0)
    let accumulator := s.accumulator + if wrong then reply.direction else 0
    let violated := s.violated || wrong
    if h : s.cursor.val + 1 < P.count then
      { s with accumulator := accumulator, violated := violated, cursor := ⟨_, h⟩ }
    else if violated then
      { s with
        point := s.point + (η / (P.count : ℝ)) • accumulator +
          P.noiseScale • P.noise.sample s.batch s.seed
        accumulator := 0
        violated := false
        cursor := ⟨0, P.count.pos⟩
        batch := s.batch + 1 }
    else { s with frozen := true }

def family (P : Public)
    (A : Algorithm (Query P) (Reply P.dimension) (Weights P.dimension)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (η : ℝ) (seed : A.Seed → P.noise.Ω) (view : A.State → ScanState P),
    0 < η ∧ Measurable seed ∧ (A.law : Measure A.Seed).map seed = P.noise.law ∧
    (∀ ω, view (A.initial ω) = initial P (seed ω)) ∧
    (∀ s, A.query s = (0, (view s).cursor, (view s).point)) ∧
    (∀ s reply, view (A.update s reply) = scanUpdate P η (view s) reply) ∧
    (∀ s, A.output s = (view s).point)

noncomputable def spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance := Data
  Query := Query
  Reply P := Reply P.dimension
  Output P := Weights P.dimension
  publicInput := Params.input
  valid p := 0 < p.input.margin ∧ p.input.margin ≤ p.input.radius ∧
    0 < p.input.noiseScale ∧ 0 < p.failure ∧ p.failure < 1 ∧
    StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID p.input.noise.sample
      (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian (Weights p.input.dimension)) p.input.noise.law
  admissible p data oracle :=
    (∃ u : Features p.input.dimension, ‖u‖ = 1 ∧
      ∀ i, ‖data i‖ ≤ p.input.radius ∧ p.input.margin ≤ ⟪u, data i⟫) ∧
    ∀ history query seed, oracle.answer history query seed = answer (data query.2.1) query.2.2
  successful p data output law :=
    (law : Measure _) {ω | ¬Separates data (output ω)} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal p.failure
  allowedAlgorithm := family

end LongTails.Setups.NoisyBatchQuadraticPerceptron
